manuscript_sha256.description: sha256 of the audited manuscript's bytes — the case folder's content identity. Absent on manifests written before content hashing, which fall back to comparing the file name.

boundary_ambiguous.description: True when the reference label occurred more than once before the next reference, so the entry's start is a guess. Such an entry is never resolved: nothing derived from its text may be trusted to name a paper.

title_check.description: Whether anyone established that the retrieved or provided file is the paper the reference names. 'unverifiable' (e.g. a scanned first page) is not 'verified' and must never be reported as a match.

supplements.description: Supplementary files the user supplied for this reference, each judged as its own document. Only ever non-empty when the reference itself is available: a supplement with no article behind it is set aside rather than allowed to stand in for the cited source. Absent on manifests written before 0.6.0, where it means none were supplied. Note that no supplement carries a title_check — a supplement's own title does not match its parent's, so the identity check that guards every article cannot apply, and these are attached on a filename match alone.

slug.description: The id this document is read, ingested and cropped under: ingest/<slug>/ and sources_resolved/<slug>.pdf. Derived from the file stem and never from an ordinal position in the folder, so removing one file cannot silently re-point another document's stored verdicts.

pdf_path.description: Local path to the supplementary PDF, as supplied by the user.

verified.description: Did anything establish that this file belongs to the reference it is attached to? True when the file's own title or DOI named that work. False when it was attached because its FILENAME carried the reference's tokens — a guess nobody checked. Absent on manifests written before 0.6.0, meaning false. The report distinguishes the two rather than warning about both equally.

references_resumed.description: True when the reference list was picked up again after an intervening section, so the entry numbering spans a boundary the parser chose to cross. Gated on block type and run length, but still a judgement — the reader should be able to check it.

reference_source.description: Which reading of the reference list these entries came from: the publisher's list deposited with Crossref, or the tool's own parse of the PDF text. Absent on manifests written before reconciliation, which are all parses.

numbering_verified.description: True when the chosen list accounts for exactly the labels the manuscript's body cites AND no entry in it refuses its own label. The second condition is not redundant: a refused entry keeps a positional label, so the extent check is satisfied by exactly the labels in doubt. The label is the join key between a claim and its source, so an unverified numbering means a verdict may be about a different paper than the label names. Absent on older manifests, which never checked.

numbering_note.description: Why the numbering was or was not confirmed, in the reader's terms — the counts each reading produced and what the body cites.

unverified_from.description: The first citation label from which the numbering is in doubt, or null when it is not in doubt. 1 means 'from the very start', which is what a single unchecked reading warrants: one candidate gives no evidence about where it went wrong.

numbering_contested.description: The two readings of the bibliography stop describing the same paper at or below a label the body cites, even though the chosen reading matched the body's labels — so the other reading either names a different work at an entry some verdict rests on, or ends before reaching it. NOT 'the other reading failed the extent check': a deposit identical for every cited label and longer by two references nobody cites fails that. Absent on manifests written before 0.7.

numbering_ledger.description: The labels the PARSED list carries, against the labels the body cites: which are duplicated, and which are carried by no entry. Always about the parsed list, even on a `reference_source: "crossref"` run where `entries` holds the deposit instead — which is exactly the case a reader inspects this for. Absent means never computed, not that nothing was dropped. Nothing is required: a reader must treat any key as possibly missing.

labels_detected.description: How many distinct bracketed numeric labels the body cites. Only that style can be read, so 0 means 'none readable', not 'none cited'.

labels_max.description: The highest label the body cites. Under citation-order numbering the list should be exactly this long.

labels_absent.description: Labels from 1 to `labels_max` that the body never cites — a hole in the body's own citing, not in the parse.

entries_parsed.description: How many entries the PDF parse produced.

numerals_distinct.description: How many distinct labels those parsed entries carry. Lower than `entries_parsed` means at least one label is duplicated.

numerals_duplicated.description: Labels carried by more than one parsed entry. A difference of two totals cannot reveal a duplicate at all.

numerals_absent.description: Labels from 1 to `labels_max` carried by no parsed entry. Only visible where the printed numerals survived the converter: three of the four parse paths label by position, and a positional run has no gaps by construction.

manuscript_supplements.description: Supplementary material belonging to the AUDITED paper, supplied with --supplement. Deliberately not an entry in `entries`: it answers for no citation label, so putting it there would inflate the reference total and let a claim citing a number be handed the paper's own appendix. Absent on manifests written before 0.6.0.

slug.description: The id this document is read, ingested and cropped under, derived from the file stem.

pdf_path.description: Local path to the supplementary PDF, as supplied by the user.
